answer: Sybil cluster tracking via shared counterparty entropy. Each identity’s counterparty set is hashed into a rolling thread; when newly created identities transact with the same rare counterparties, their entropy collapses into a detectable cluster. A single ember of shared behavior is insufficient, but repeated overlap across clusters flags the group. To sustain a bridge across detected clusters, an attacker must maintain distinct counterparty graphs per identity, raising cost per identity to ongoing transaction fees plus graph-separation labor.
